# Relax Motion

**Status:** Not yet tested on hardware.

**Credit:** Reverse engineering by [kristofferR](https://github.com/kristofferR/ha-adjustable-bed).

## Known Models

The app's numeric advertisement model selects the controls. Similar names can
have different capabilities. Both three-actuator layouts expose back, lumbar
and legs; neither establishes a separate head-tilt actuator.

Other supplied numeric identities use the app's basic two-actuator layout:
P1 at 450 or below, P2 above 450. A missing identity never selects a model.

## Features

| Feature | Supported |
|---------|-----------|
| Motor control | Back / legs, optional lumbar, or combined actuator |
| Position feedback | No measured position or angle |
| Memory | P1: up to five on models with a memory editor; P2 model 500: one |
| Massage | P1, model and app-page dependent; head/foot intensity 1–3 with separate off controls |
| Lights | P1, model-dependent brightness 0–255 and explicit off |
| Sensed-light timer | P1, 10–6000 seconds in steps of 10, including models without a light tile |
| Snore intervention settings | P1, unlocked by a positive sleep-state reply |
| Side addressing | None; two receivers can be combined as separate physical beds |
| Clock / alarm | No direct BLE clock or alarm command |

## Protocol Details

**Advertised service:** `6e403587-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e`.

**Write and notify characteristics:** Discovered from properties, not fixed UUIDs.
For numeric identities above 450, prefer that service, otherwise use the first
returned service. For other identities, use the last service when primary,
otherwise the first primary service (or the first service if none is primary).
Use the last write-capable characteristic in that service and subscribe to every
notify/indicate characteristic. A previous session's destination is never reused.

### Packet Format

P1 is eight bytes: U8 sequence, U8 PID, LE16 command, LE32 parameter. Sequence
wraps at 256. Builder calls consume sequence numbers, so gaps are valid. There
is no checksum or authentication handshake. Motor endpoints are raw 0 and
10000; those values do not establish angles or percentages.

P2 normal frames are nine bytes: `EE 01 05`, BE32 mask, parameter byte, `C0`.
P2 extra frames use `EE 02 05`, U8 command, BE24 tag, value byte, `C0`.
They carry no side address, checksum or encryption. Release is exactly five
zero bytes, not a nine-byte zero-mask frame. Its physical efficacy is unverified.

### Write Mode

The app leaves the discovered Android write type unchanged. Home Assistant
uses acknowledged writes when the characteristic supports them, otherwise
write without response. Completion is transport delivery, not bed confirmation.
The app's MTU request of 500 does not establish a firmware requirement; Home
Assistant manages its Bluetooth transport and connection setup.

## Detection / Setup

Search for **Relax Motion app**. Keep the numeric model captured from the
advertisement, or enter the number shown in the app. No model is inferred from
the shared service or a similar product name. The discovery candidate requires
a nonempty Bluetooth name and the shared service first in the advertised list.
Names starting with `ZKYL-` belong to the separate network setup route.

The selected scanner includes the manufacturer company bytes. Model identity
is the first byte, except when it is 89 and there are more than four bytes:
then add bytes 0, 2, 3 and 4. Company records are ordered numerically before
that calculation. Keep the saved number across reconnects.

The normal **Relax Motion** page uses P2 only above 450. **Older motor page**
keeps P1 for every supplied number and uses the first advertisement byte.
The two **Cheers alternative page** choices represent an app-name-dependent
branch, separate from the CheersSleep app integration. Choose one only when
your app actually uses that page and label language. It always uses P1 while
GATT service selection still follows the numeric identity.

P1 memory editors can extend the initial model count to five. P2 exposes only
the shown model-500 memory row, including its reachable edit/save operation.
An unused create-memory method does not establish more P2 slots. Arbitrary
manually altered app storage is not a hardware capability declaration.

## Position Feedback / Notifications

P1 recognizes CID `1201`, PID `82` and an LE32 value strictly between 0 and 4
as a positive sleep-state reply. It accepts trailing data. Wrong PID or an
out-of-range value gives false; truncated unrelated packets are ignored safely.
A positive reply enables snore settings for the rest of that connection, even
if a later reply is false. Snore interval is 0–120 minutes, sent as seconds.
The snore switch and setting numbers show assumed values only after delivery;
partial delivery makes them unknown. Disconnect clears session state.

P2 has no notification parser, measured positions or inferred accessory state.

## Command Timing

P1 sends a global STOP before a main-page movement or tool, waits 200 ms
(the app's non-Android interval), and sends the command once. Held movement
ends with global STOP. Editor-specific axis STOP buttons are also available.
Memory saves are immediate. The sleep-state query follows notification setup
after 200 ms, or 1500 ms on the alternative page.

P2 movement refreshes every 100 ms. Native execution drains its initial STOP
pair before movement, and always ends with release writes separated by 100 ms.
A preset has an initial release pair and dispatches at 300 ms; its command
is sent at offsets 0, 100 and 200 ms, followed by release at 400 and 500 ms.
A memory save uses that burst without the initial preparation.

Finite holds must exceed the dispatch preparation: 200 ms for P1 and 300 ms
for P2. Shorter requests are rejected before movement.

All waits and refreshes belong to the running command. STOP, cancellation,
controller replacement and disconnection prevent later queued movement.
In-flight writes and required release cleanup settle before the wire is handed
back. Retries are bounded by Home Assistant instead of copying the app's
unbounded retry timers.

## Notes

The alternative page's massage and memory paths compare Chinese labels.
English labels leave the memory list empty and do not establish usable zone
massage controls; the global massage-off fallback remains available. Model 32's rhythm changes zone actions to strength commands;
turning rhythm off restores normal intensity actions. Intensity numbers show unknown
until their level is sent, and reset when the rhythm mode or connection changes. Comfort sleep is
conditional on the alternative model profile; off uses motor STOP, not the
unused comfort-off constant. The alternative page also has a translator
initialization defect, so these conditional branches do not establish that its
UI works on a real device.

Wi-Fi setup, credentials, network status, cloud accounts, device administration,
OTA, media and unrelated reporting are outside this integration's bed controls.
Hardware captures can confirm GATT properties, actuator mapping, security and
release efficacy without changing those product boundaries.

### Evidence

Based on Relax Motion 1.5.0 (521), `com.motion.rmtrelax`.
